## Fixed: the Linux build starts on Ubuntu 24.04 and older again

UltraLog 3.1.1 for Linux would not start on Ubuntu 24.04, 22.04, Debian 12 or most other distributions. It stopped with `version 'GLIBC_2.43' not found`, because it had been built on a newer system than the one it was meant to run on ([#113](https://github.com/ClassicMiniDIY/UltraLog/issues/113)).

3.2.0 runs on any Linux with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora 36+), as 3.1.0 did. Each release build now checks this before it is published, so it cannot happen again unnoticed.

### Linux: install 3.2.0 by hand once

- **3.1.1 never started for you:** download `ultralog-linux.tar.gz` below and install 3.2.0 by hand. 3.1.1 could not start, so it could not update itself.
- **Still on 3.1.0 or older:** install by hand once too (see the 3.1.1 notes). Updates after that install from the app.
- Windows and macOS: nothing to do; update from the app as usual.

## New: color the scatter plot by a third channel

Each scatter plot can now color its cells by another channel instead of the hit count: AFR or lambda over RPM × MAP, knock or EGT over RPM × load, and so on ([#114](https://github.com/ClassicMiniDIY/UltraLog/issues/114)).

- **Z Axis** in the Tool Properties panel: **Hits** (as before) or any channel, set separately for the left and right plot.
- **Cell value:** **Mean**, **Min** or **Max** of that channel's samples in each cell. For AFR or lambda, Min shows the richest and Max the leanest reading, so a lean spot is not hidden in an average. The scatter plot keeps 512 cells per axis, much finer than the Histogram.
- **Color range:** automatic, or a fixed range you type (for example 0.75 – 1.25 λ) to compare both plots, or two logs, on the same scale. Values on both sides of zero, such as a lambda-error channel, use a color map centered on zero.
- Hovering a cell or clicking it shows the Z value and how many samples it covers.

### Also in this release

- The scatter plot's X, Y and Z lists now include computed channels.
- PNG and PDF exports of the scatter plots count and color cells by the same rules as the screen (on a coarser grid), and each plot gets its own color scale when the two differ.
- Missing samples no longer pile up at the edge of a scatter plot, and removing a computed channel no longer leaves a scatter plot showing a different channel.
- For Claude Desktop (MCP): `show_scatter_plot` takes optional `z_channel` and `z_stat` (`mean`, `min` or `max`).

The [User Guide](https://github.com/ClassicMiniDIY/UltraLog/wiki/User-Guide#scatter-plot-tool) has the updated Scatter Plot section.
